course_description:
This course explores the role of social media platforms in generating engagement, managing brands and promoting products, services and causes. We critically examine the promotional culture of social media platforms and consider competing frameworks for understanding their benefits and drawbacks. Trends in the development of social media, their participatory cultures, and their uses by organisations are examine. Students create a social media strategy and work towards developing and curating social media content on social media platforms such as YouTube, TikTok, Twitter, Google, Snap Chat and Facebook. Students use analytics tools that enable organisations to track real time metrics related to engagement and sentiment.

Social media is rapidly becoming central to all forms of human communication and connection.

The mobile phone and its signals now play a vital role in facilitating our entertainment, work and information sharing practices.

In this course students engage in critical conversations about the advantages and disadvantages of social media in our lives as they acquire new skills and proficiencies.

Designed in consultation with extensive industry input this course is structured in three modules – create, promote & evaluate. ﾠ

Students build upon their practical skills as they create engaging and effective content, use promotional techniques to attract attention and evaluate the success of their campaigns using analytical dashboards and tools.

Students work with industry as to gain knowledge and practical experience and insights as they consider how advances in algorithmic technology, mobile phones and AI techniques play an important role in shaping all aspects of communication practice.

As students enrolled in this course use social media tools to create content it is important that they are able to easily access a range of social media platforms in order to complete the assessment tasks and fulfill the learning objectives.

course_aims: This course aims to introduce students to key social media theory as they acquire tangible skills in content production and dissemination. Students learn how to create strategic campaigns, and to create, promote and evaluate their social media outputs with the guidance of industry experts.

learning_outcomes.description: Apply promotional theory and strategic thinking to analyze case studies and design campaigns for specific target audiences.
Utilize social media tools to create multi-modal content that prioritizes clarity, concision, and high audience engagement.
Evaluate social media campaigns and peer performance using industry-specific metrics and tools.
Collaborate with colleagues to pitch communication solutions via structured oral presentations.
Defend strategic communication choices and demonstrate subject knowledge during live, spontaneous questioning.
Critically reflect on key industry themes, personal development, and individual contributions to group environments

assessment_details.title: CREATE: Video & Oral Presentation and Groupwork Reflection
assessment_details.task_description: Assessment 1: (Create) Video & Oral presentation and Evaluation (30%) Part A: Video Presentation – due in week 5 tutorial 2026 Part B: Oral Presentation – due in week 5 tutorial 2026 Part C: Groupwork Evaluation – due 28 August 2026 @4pm Weighting: Part A 15% Group, Part B 10%, Individual Part C 5%Individual (30% Overall) _______________________________________________________________________________________ There are three parts to this assignment – Part A, Part B and Part C. Part A- Video Presentation (15 marks): Part A is a group task, and Part B and Part C are individual tasks. All tasks must be completed to pass Assessment 1. In groups of 4-5, you will create a TikTok or Instagram reel series (3 x two-minute reels) designed to educate a specific target audience about promotional culture. You will present this in a “thought leadership” style. In your groups you will select a current social media example that is applicable to course concepts from weeks 1-4 (which are all aspects of promotional culture). In your videos, you will analyse the example through the lens of relevant theory by demonstrating engagement with specific readings from the course content from weeks 1-4. In industry settings, it is standard procedure to work with colleagues that you don’t know. Use this task as an opportunity to practise working professionally alongside your ‘colleagues.’ You will present your videos in class during the Week 5 tutorial. Then, you will undertake Part B which consists of an oral presentation and Q&A where you must discuss the rationale behind your video. Part B- Oral presentation (10 marks): Each student will receive an individual mark for Part B, determined partly by performance and partly by the quality of their response to spontaneous questions. After Part A, in the Week 5 tutorial you will give an oral presentation with your group where you will explain your rationale for the videos. All group members will be expected to speak for approximately two (2) minutes for a total presentation time of 8-10 minutes and respond to questions from the tutor. You do not need to create any slides/visual aids for this. Each group should cover the following aspects in your rationale Target audience : who is the target audience for this video? Strategy : what is your overarching plan? Goal : what are you trying to get your target audience to do or think? Objectives : what are you hoping to achieve through this video? For example, comments, likes, shares, click-throughs, views etc. Key Message : what is the message you want your viewers to take away? What do you want them to think about or discuss with friends? What change in behaviour or thinking are you trying to influence? Tactics : What is your communication and creative tactic to reach and engage this target audience? Theory : You need to meaningfully, verbally reference at least two relevant course readings/sources Part C- Groupwork Evaluation (5 marks): By Friday 4pm of Week 5, you must answer specific prompts about group engagement throughout the planning and production of your video series. Your responses should total 150 words. This will be submitted via Blackboard. Questions: What were the strengths of your group dynamic? What were some challenges you faced throughout the groupwork process? How did you resolve these challenges? What would you do differently in future groupwork settings? Recording of Oral and Practical Assessment All presentations will be recorded for marking purposes via recording facilities available where the assessment takes place (eg. ECHO360, Zoom, camera device) Recordings will be retained by the School of Communication and Arts for at least 12 months from the release of the final grade for the course. Recordings will be stored in a secure manner and will only be accessed by authorised school staff for the purposes of: Moderation of marking; Provision of feedback to the student(s) recorded; and/or Re-marking following a successful re-mark application. assessment_details.title: PROMOTE: Case Study Analysis & Peer Engagement
assessment_details.task_description: Assessment 2: (Promote) Case Study Analysis & Peer Engagement Part A: Case Study Presentation – due in week 6-9 tutorials 2026 Part B: Peer Engagement – due in due in week 6-9 tutorials 2026 Weighting: Part A 20% Individual & Part B 15% Individual (35% Overall) _______________________________________________________________________________________ There are two parts to this assignment – Part A and Part B. Both parts are individual tasks. Part A- Case Study Presentation (20 marks): For Part A, in tutorials from Weeks 6–9 you will be allocated to present during one of your regularly scheduled tutorial sessions. Your presentation will be based on that week’s topic (e.g. self-branding, influencer culture, etc.). Alongside the other students presenting in your tutorial, you will deliver a 10-minute presentation. Afterwards, you will lead a 5-minute Q&A discussion. You must create one (1) slide that clearly presents your key analytical points and lists your references. For this task, you must select your own case study in which a social media creator engages in self-branding practices in partnership with a brand. Drawing on the course lectures and readings for your allocated week, you are required to critically analyse the creator’s use of self-branding and examine how it aligns with the associated brand. Make sure you are familiar with the readings ahead of time. There is no expectation that you argue whether the partnership was “good” or “bad”; rather, the focus is on applying course concepts thoughtfully and critically to your chosen example . Depending on your analysis, your presentation may function as a critique of influencer culture, an evaluation of promotional strategies, or an exploration of branding and identity practices within digital media culture. Your analysis should also identify and evaluate at least two ethical dimensions of your topic through social, cultural and/or political lenses. To do this, your presentation must demonstrate meaningful engagement with at least two course readings , as well as any additional relevant sources you have independently identified. You will also be graded on how thoughtfully you answer questions from peers and your tutor about your presentation. The idea is for you to facilitate a meaningful discussion based on your expertise of your specific case study. Part B- Peer Engagement (15 marks): Part B occurs while other students are presenting for their Part A. When you are not presenting (including before or after your own presentation), you will be given a worksheet where you must respond to your peers’ presentations through handwritten commentary (in response to provided questions) as they are presenting . You will use your written commentary to engage in the Q&A session with the student who presented. You must take a photo of your completed worksheet and upload it to Blackboard by 4pm . It will be graded on how you: Demonstrate meaningful and nuanced engagement with peers’ presentations Demonstrate knowledge of course content Your tutor will collect your worksheets at the end of tutorials. Your best 2/4 worksheets will be counted towards your grade. assessment_details.task_description: Part A: AV Presentation and Q&A – due in week 12 tutorial 2026 Part B: Evaluation Report – due 4pm on day of tutorial presentation 2026 Part C: Peer Evaluation – due 23 October 2026 @4pm Weighting: Part A 20% Group, Part B 10% Group & Part C 5% Individual (35% Overall) _______________________________________________________________________________________ There are three parts to this assignment – Part A, Part B and Part C. Part A and B are group tasks and Part C is an individual task. Part A – AV Presentation and Q&A (20 marks): In this assignment, you will be provided with performance data from a communications campaign and, working in groups of 4–5, take on the role of a consultancy that has implemented the campaign. You will analyse its performance and translate insights into actionable client recommendations. Groups will be randomly allocated as in professional settings. This task develops your ability to evaluate performance data, make informed decisions, and demonstrate value to clients and stakeholders. Post-campaign evaluation is a critical component of contemporary social media and digital marketing practice. You will present your findings as industry professionals, using campaign results to justify strategic decisions and propose future directions—reflecting real-world agency practice. Your group will use the provided PowerPoint template to present your key insights and findings in an audio-visual industry-style report deck . The deck should communicate your evaluation and recommendations clearly and professionally, as though it were being presented to a client. Your presentation should include: An evaluation of both Organic and Paid channel performance against the original campaign objectives (e.g. were targets met across key metrics including reach, engagement, click-throughs, conversions, etc.) An assessment of how evolving platform conditions such as algorithm changes or shifts in search behaviour may have influenced campaign performance and how results are measured Strategic recommendations and next steps for future campaigns, evidenced directly by your analysis of the performance data Walkthrough of the overall campaign performance, your evaluation, and your recommendations Your video presentation should be 10 minutes, and all groups will exhibit their video in the Week 12 tutorial. All group members need to prepare for a 5-minute Q&A discussion with the tutor after the video has been exhibited. You will be assessed on how well as a group you: Critically evaluate the provided data Utilise industry sources to support your evaluation Use campaign performance evaluation to inform future recommendations Align with compelling industry design standards How well you respond to questions Part B- Evaluation Report (10 marks): Part B is a group task . Each group must submit one structured report that supports the video presentation. The structure will be provided to you, and acts as a written version of your presentation. Your report will be assessed on how you follow industry structure and style and communicate with clarity. Part C- Groupwork Evaluation (5 marks): Part C is an individual task. By Friday 4pm of Week 12, you must answer specific prompts about group engagement throughout the planning and production of your video series. Your responses should total 150 words. learning_activities.topic: Module 1 CREATE: Week 1 Lecture (Recording) The lecture this week will be delivered as a video recording so that students can rewatch critical information on the assessment and course content. Content will cover how brands, governments, not-for-profit organisations and government policies shape advertising and media promotion. It is vital that students complete course readings and watch the first animated video on 'promotional culture' this week to prepare for assessment one. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L06

Module 1 CREATE: Week 1: No tutorial this week There is no activity this week. It is important that students complete the course reading in preparation for assessment one. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L06

Module 1 CREATE: Week 2 Lecture (Recording) The lecture this week will be delivered as a video recording so that students can rewatch different examples of promotional culture in preparation for assessment one. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L06
Module 1 CREATE: Week 2 Tutorial Students allocated to groups for assignment 1. Students start planning for assessment task. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L06
Module 1 CREATE: Week 3 Lecture (In Person) Students identify the difference between platforms and forms of participation and creative expression available to users. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L06
Module 1 CREATE: Week 3 Tutorial Students work together in groups to respond to assessment 1. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L06

Module 1 CREATE: Week 4 Lecture (In Person) This seminar looks at the concept of labour and the work users perform when they engage with social media platforms, and how this differs from more traditional forms of media such as television. The relationship between labour and self-branding is explored. Learning outcomes: L01, L02

Module 1 CREATE: Week 4 Tutorial Students work in groups to finalise teamwork in preparation for in class presentations. Students are allocated individual presentation times and topics for Assignment 2 presentations, beginning next week. Learning outcomes: L01, L02
Module 2 PROMOTE: Week 5 Lecture (In Person) This lecture considers the notion of self branding and how it relates to the promotional culture of social media. Learning outcomes: L03
Module 2 PROMOTE: Week 5 Tutorial Assignment 1 in class presentations. Learning outcomes: L03

Module 2 PROMOTE: Week 6 Lecture (In Person) In this lecture we critically consider how brands draw on the self branding practices of influencers and creators to promote brands. Learning outcomes: L03
Module 2 PROMOTE: Week 6 Tutorial In class individual students give presentations and lead discussion on the course content. Learning outcomes: L03

Module 2 PROMOTE: Week 7 Lecture (In Person) In this lecture we will consider different campaigns and their use of creators and influencers and what constitutes good industry practice. Learning outcomes: L03
Module 2 PROMOTE: Week 7 Tutorial In class individual students give presentations and lead discussion on the course content. Learning outcomes: L03
Module 2 PROMOTE: Week 8 Lecture (In Person) This lecture looks at the AIMCO code of ethics and the rules surrounding the use of influencers to endorse brands. Learning outcomes: L03
Module 2 PROMOTE: Week 8 Tutorial In class individual students give presentations and lead discussion on the course content. Learning outcomes: L04, L05

Module 3 EVALUATE: Week 9 Lecture (In Person) In this lecture students will be presented with the case study for assignment three and will learn about how to assess a campaign using metrics. Learning outcomes: L04, L05
